title: French Onion Soup
subtitle: Slow-caramelised onion soup with Gruyère croutons
excerpt: Sweet, deeply caramelised onions simmered in beef stock and wine, ladled into bowls and topped with toasted bread blanketed in melted Gruyère. One of the great soups of the world.

recipe.sourceNotes: French onion soup (soupe à l'oignon) has been made in France since at least the 18th century and is strongly associated with the markets of Les Halles in Paris, where it was served as a restorative soup to market workers in the early hours of the morning. The recipe is deceptively simple — onions, stock, bread, and cheese — but the quality of the result depends almost entirely on the patience with which the onions are caramelised. They should spend at least 45 minutes over medium-low heat, turning from pale and translucent to deep mahogany brown with a concentrated, sweet flavour. Rushing this stage is the most common mistake. Gruyère is the classic cheese; Comté makes an equally good alternative.

content.text: The onions take time. Start with a high heat to drive off the water, then reduce to medium-low and stir every few minutes for 45 to 50 minutes. They will seem to take forever then suddenly turn deep brown all at once. Do not rush this or add sugar to shortcut: properly caramelised onions have a complexity that hurried ones do not. The bread should be toasted until completely dry so it holds its shape in the soup rather than dissolving.

Melt the butter and oil together in a large, wide pot over medium-high heat. Add all the onions and cook, stirring frequently, for 10 minutes until wilted. Reduce to medium-low. Add the garlic, thyme, bay, and a pinch of salt. Cook for 45 to 50 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the onions are deep golden brown.

Pour in the wine. Increase the heat and let it bubble for 2 minutes, scraping up the sticky residue from the base of the pan. Add the stock, remaining salt, and pepper. Simmer for 20 minutes. Remove the thyme and bay. Taste and adjust seasoning.

Heat the grill to high. Ladle the hot soup into 4 oven-proof bowls. Float a slice of dry-toasted bread on each. Pile the Gruyère thickly over the bread. Grill for 3 to 4 minutes until bubbling and dark golden in patches. Serve immediately.
